title: Can Do Descriptors
tableHeader: By the end of each of the given levels of English language proficiency* English language learners can...
footnote: *Except for Level 6, for which there is no ceiling.

sources.frameworkPdf: WIDA English Language Development Standards Framework, 2020 Edition

keyUseDefinitions.text: Narrate highlights language to convey real or imaginary experiences through stories and histories. Narratives serve many purposes, including to instruct, entertain, teach, or support argumentation.
Inform highlights language to provide factual information. As students convey information, they define, describe, compare, contrast, organize, categorize, or classify concepts, ideas, or phenomena.

Recount: To display knowledge or narrate experiences or events. Example tasks for the Key Use of Recount include telling or summarizing stories, producing information reports, and sharing past experiences. WIDA 2020 splits Recount into Narrate and Inform.

keyUseDefinitions.text2016: Explain: To clarify the "why" or the "how" of ideas, actions, or phenomena. Example tasks include describing life cycles, sharing why or how things work, stating causes and effects, and sharing results of experiments.
keyUseDefinitions.text: Explain highlights language to give an account for how things work or why things happen. As students explain, they substantiate the inner workings of natural, man-made, and social phenomena.

keyUseDefinitions.text2016: Argue: To persuade by making claims supported by evidence. Example tasks include stating preferences or opinions and constructing arguments with evidence.
keyUseDefinitions.text: Argue highlights language to justify claims using evidence and reasoning. Argue can be used to advance or defend an idea or solution, change the audience’s point of view, bring about action, or accept a position or evaluation of an issue.

Discuss: To interact with others to build meaning and share knowledge. Example tasks include participating in small or large group activities and projects. In 2020, Discuss is not a genre family; it is threaded through all Key Language Uses.

keyLanguageUses.mapping: WIDA 2020: Recount has been separated into Narrate and Inform. Discuss is not a genre family; it is threaded throughout all Key Language Uses. Level Can Do bullets in this file still come from the 2016 Grades 6-8 Can Do booklet (Recount / Explain / Argue / Discuss).
keyLanguageUses.overlapNote: Key Language Uses can overlap and inform each other. They are not strict walls. This session still has ONE primary key_use — write the passage and task for that use. Do not invent new Can Do bullets.

Narrate.tableDefinition: Represent experiences through stories and histories.
Narrate.definition: Narrate highlights language to convey real or imaginary experiences through stories and histories. Narratives serve many purposes, including to instruct, entertain, teach, or support argumentation.
genres: imaginative stories (short story, mystery, science fiction, fantasy)
gradeBand6_8: Describe people, objects, and scenes using imagery, metaphors, and other stylistic devices
Manipulate pace to bring attention to key points in the narrative
Interpret and use historical narratives as primary source evidence in constructing arguments
contentMust: Main purpose: a story or history — what happened, who was involved, where and when.
Use sequence of events. At this grade band, mark why an event matters when the level allows it.
contentMustNot: Do not make the main text a fact report that only defines or classifies (that is Inform).
Do not make how/why a system works the main purpose (that is Explain).
Do not make a claim plus evidence the main purpose (that is Argue).

Inform.tableDefinition: Communicate factual information on a topic.
Inform.definition: Inform highlights language to provide factual information. As students convey information, they define, describe, compare, contrast, organize, categorize, or classify concepts, ideas, or phenomena.
genres: lab, investigation, design, or problem-solution reports
gradeBand6_8: Manage information about entities according to their composition, taxonomies, and classifications
Identify and describe various relationships among ideas and information
Interpret multiple sources of information to develop knowledge before reporting on topics
Construct research reports that require multiple sources of factual information
contentMust: Main purpose: facts about a topic — define, describe, compare, classify, or report.
Stay objective. Information reports describe or classify (e.g. types of clouds); they do not explain how clouds form (Explain).
contentMustNot: Do not make a plotted story the main text (that is Narrate).
Do not make how/why the main purpose (that is Explain).
Do not make a claim plus evidence the main purpose (that is Argue).

Explain.tableDefinition: Give account for how or why things work.
Explain.definition: Explain highlights language to give an account for how things work or why things happen. As students explain, they substantiate the inner workings of natural, man-made, and social phenomena.
genres: sequential, causal, cyclical, factorial, or consequential explanations
gradeBand6_8: Identify, analyze, and give account for causal, consequential, or systems relationships
Apply scientific reasoning to show how or why something works
Construct explanations using models or representations
Use evidence in the construction of scientific explanations
contentMust: Main purpose: how or why — cause, process, or system.
Explanations are more than descriptions: not only what, but how/why.
contentMustNot: Do not only name or classify without how/why (that is Inform).
Do not make a story the main purpose (that is Narrate).
Do not make persuading with a claim the main purpose (that is Argue).

Argue.tableDefinition: Justify one’s claims using evidence and reasoning.
Argue.definition: Argue highlights language to justify claims using evidence and reasoning. Argue can be used to advance or defend an idea or solution, change the audience’s point of view, bring about action, or accept a position or evaluation of an issue.
gradeBand6_8: Interpret multiple sources of information to develop claims and counterclaims
Construct claims and offer them for debate
Contextualize and evaluate primary and secondary sources
contentMust: Main purpose: a claim plus reasons or evidence the student can hear or read.
At this grade band, include a counterclaim when the level allows it.
contentMustNot: Do not only tell what happened (Narrate) or only list facts (Inform).
Do not only explain a process without a position (Explain).
